final_writeup:
I do not resolve the limiting assertion. I obtain two exact reformulations, finite-n probability bounds, and a concrete example showing why the quoted a.a.s. 3-colorability theorem is insufficient.

Orienting each Hamilton cycle cyclically changes the requested coefficient only by an overall sign. After dividing out ∏x_v², the coefficient becomes the constant term of ∏_{u→v}(1-x_v/x_u). Hence it is the signed enumerator of balanced subsets of the directed arcs.

A stronger reformulation uses a primitive cube root ζ. Root-of-unity filtering is exact because every variable has degree at most four and 2 is the unique exponent in {0,...,4} congruent to 2 modulo 3. For a proper coloring c:[n]→Z/3Z and a min-label-oriented edge u<v, put ε_c(u,v)=+1 when c(v)-c(u)=1 and -1 when it is -1. The identity
ζ^a-ζ^b=(ζ-ζ²)ε(a,b)ζ^{-(a+b)}
shows that all phases cancel because every vertex has degree four. Thus
A_n=(-1)^n Σ_c ∏_{uv∈E(G_n)} ε_c(u,v),
where the sum is over proper 3-colorings and includes edge multiplicity.

Global permutations of the three colors preserve each total sign, and their action on proper colorings is free. Consequently A_n/6 is, up to (-1)^n, the number of positive color-orbits minus the number of negative color-orbits. In particular, an odd number of color-orbits certifies A_n≠0. Exact cancellation really occurs: for C1=(1,2,3,4,5,6,7) and C2=(1,4,5,3,6,7,2), there are twelve proper colorings, forming two orbits of opposite signs, and A_7=0.

After fixing the first cycle, define W_ab=0 if a=b, +1 if b-a=1 mod 3, and -1 otherwise, and f(c)=∏_i W_{c_i,c_{i+1}}. For a uniform coordinate permutation π, the orientation-normalized coefficient is
X_π=<f,U_πf>.
It has exactly the same absolute value and zero event as A_n. Moreover ||f||²=q_n=2^n+2(-1)^n.

Projection onto coordinate-permutation invariants gives the rigorous moment bound
E[A_n²]=E[X_π²] >= 6q_n²/3^n.
Since |X_π|<=q_n, this implies
Pr[A_n≠0] >= 6/3^n
for every n. For even n, the nonnegative normalized mean yields the stronger bound Pr[A_n≠0]>=4/(2^n+2). These bounds decay and therefore do not establish the desired limit.

Finally, the balanced-subset formula reduces each coefficient to a signed sum indexed by vertex sets compatible with both cyclic orders. A fixed 2k-set is compatible with probability 1/binom(2k-1,k). Thus the expected number of nonempty compatible sets is
Σ_{k>=1} binom(n,2k)/binom(2k-1,k),
whose exponential growth rate is 3/2. This gives an exact combinatorial starting point for the missing anti-concentration argument.

Using the a.a.s. 3-colorability result quoted in the supplied text, failure of the target is, up to o(1), precisely exact equality between the numbers of positive and negative nonempty coloring-orbits. None of the bounds above controls that equality with probability tending to zero, so neither FULL resolution nor a disproof of the limit is claimed.

results.claim: After cyclically orienting both Hamilton cycles, the coefficient B in the directed product satisfies B=Σ_H(-1)^|H|, where H ranges over arc subsets with indegree_H(v)=outdegree_H(v) at every vertex; the requested A equals ±B.
results.proof_sketch: Each vertex is the tail of exactly two directed factors. Hence the directed product divided by ∏_v x_v² is ∏_{u→v}(1-x_v/x_u). Selecting H in its expansion gives sign (-1)^|H| and exponent indegree_H(v)-outdegree_H(v) at vertex v. Its monomial is constant exactly under the stated balance equations.

results.claim: Let T be a nonempty even vertex set. Call T compatible when the two cyclic orders induce the same alternating bipartition of T, up to swapping its two classes. Then B=(1+(-1)^n)^2+2Σ_T w(T), where the sum is over compatible T and w(T)∈{±1} is well-defined.
results.proof_sketch: Record, on every outgoing cycle arc, whether it belongs to H. Balance says that the binary strings on the two cycles change at exactly the same vertices and in opposite directions. Along either cycle, change directions alternate, giving compatibility. A compatible nonempty T produces exactly two solutions, which are simultaneous complements. Their selected-arc counts have the same parity because there are 2n arcs, so both contribute the same sign w(T). With T empty, both cycle strings are independently constant, giving (1+(-1)^n)^2.

results.claim: If N_n is the number of compatible nonempty sets, then E[N_n]=Σ_{1<=k<=n/2} binom(n,2k)/binom(2k-1,k), this expectation has exponential growth rate 3/2, and E|A_n|<=4+2E[N_n].
results.proof_sketch: For fixed T of size 2k, its alternating classes under the first cycle both have size k. The induced cyclic order under a uniform second cycle is uniform. Fixing one class member first, there are (2k-1)! cyclic orders and k!(k-1)! alternating ones, giving probability 1/binom(2k-1,k). Sum over T. The coefficient formula gives the absolute-value bound. Stirling's formula shows that a term with 2k≈qn has exponential rate exp(H(q)-q log 2), uniquely maximized at q=1/3 with value 3/2.

results.claim: For min-label-oriented edge occurrences, A_n=(-1)^n Σ_c s(c), where c ranges over proper 3-colorings and s(c)=∏_{u<v} ε_c(u,v), with ε_c(u,v)=+1 if c(v)-c(u)=1 mod 3 and -1 otherwise.
results.proof_sketch: Use the third-root filter 3^{-n}Σ_c(∏ζ^{-2c(v)})P_G(ζ^{c(1)},...,ζ^{c(n)}). It selects exactly exponent two in every variable. Nonproper colorings vanish. For a proper edge, ζ^a-ζ^b=(ζ-ζ²)ε(a,b)ζ^{-(a+b)}. Degree four makes the edge phases ζ^{-4Σc(v)} cancel the filter phase ζ^{Σc(v)}. Finally (ζ-ζ²)^{2n}/3^n=(-1)^n.

results.claim: The S_3 action on proper colorings is free and preserves s(c). Consequently A_n is divisible by 6 and A_n/6=(-1)^n(N_+-N_-), where N_± count positive and negative color-orbits. In particular, an odd total number of color-orbits forces A_n≠0.
results.proof_sketch: Cyclic color shifts preserve every ε. A color reflection reverses every edge sign, but there are 2n edge occurrences, so s(c) remains unchanged. A proper coloring uses at least two colors, and a permutation fixing two colors is the identity; hence every orbit has size six. The displayed orbit formula follows immediately, as does the parity criterion.

results.claim: Three-colorability alone does not force nonvanishing: for C1=(1,2,3,4,5,6,7) and C2=(1,4,5,3,6,7,2), the graph has 12 proper 3-colorings but A_7=0.
results.proof_sketch: Fix colors of vertices 1,2 to 0,1, selecting one representative from every S_3-orbit. The constraints force exactly two representatives: (0,1,0,1,2,1,2) and (0,1,2,1,0,1,2). Under min-label edge orientations their sign products are respectively +1 and -1: the first has four negative edge occurrences, the second five. Their two six-element orbits cancel, proving both the coloring count and A_7=0.

results.claim: If C1=C2 as undirected cycles, then A_n=(-1)^n(2^n+2(-1)^n), so A_n is nonzero for every n>=3.
results.proof_sketch: Every edge sign in the coloring formula occurs twice and therefore squares to +1. The signed sum becomes the ordinary number of proper 3-colorings of C_n, which is 2^n+2(-1)^n by the standard two-state recurrence after fixing the first color.

results.claim: For the random model, after fixing C1 by relabeling there is a fixed vector f∈{0,±1}^{3^n} and uniform π∈S_n such that |A_n|=|X_π| for X_π=<f,U_πf>, and ||f||²=q_n=2^n+2(-1)^n.
results.proof_sketch: Take f(c)=∏_iW_{c_i,c_{i+1}} with W_ab the cyclic color sign, zero on equal colors. A permutation π sends the canonical directed cycle to a uniform directed Hamilton cycle, and the signed coloring formula becomes the displayed inner product. Rotations duplicate every directed cycle equally; reversing direction or replacing directed factors by min-label factors only changes an overall sign. The squared norm counts proper colorings of C_n, giving q_n.

results.claim: The signed color-count generating polynomial is F_n(z_0,z_1,z_2)=tr((diag(z)W)^n); it is zero for odd n and equals 2(-1)^k(z_0z_1+z_0z_2+z_1z_2)^k for n=2k.
results.proof_sketch: The trace expansion is exactly the definition of f with a variable marking each color occurrence. The characteristic polynomial of diag(z)W is λ(λ²+z_0z_1+z_0z_2+z_1z_2). Its nonzero eigenvalues are opposites, so odd power traces vanish and the 2k-th power trace is twice (-1)^k times the indicated kth power.

results.claim: For even n=2k, if m_n=E_π[X_π], then m_n=4Σ_{p+q+r=k} binom(k;p,q,r)^2/binom(2k;p+q,p+r,q+r), and Pr[A_n≠0]>=m_n/(2^n+2)>=4/(2^n+2). Moreover m_n tends to 16/3.
results.proof_sketch: Averaging U_π is orthogonal projection onto functions determined by color-count vectors. Thus m_n is Σ_α S_α²/binom(n;α), where S_α is the corresponding coefficient of F_n. Substitution gives the exact sum. The constant-vector component alone has squared norm |F_n(1,1,1)|²/3^n=4, proving m_n>=4. Since |X_π|<=q_n, m_n<=q_n Pr[X_π≠0]. Finally, uniform Stirling estimates reduce the exact sum to a two-dimensional Gaussian Riemann sum; the unique entropy maximum is p=q=r=k/3 and its Gaussian integral is 16/3.

Let h=f⊗f. Then E[X_π²]=<h,Ph>=||Ph||², where P projects paired color strings onto coordinate-permutation orbits. For each σ∈S_3 and color-count vector α, consider the orbit of pairs (c,σc). If N_α proper cyclic words have counts α, this orbit contributes N_α²/binom(n;α). The six families are disjoint because a proper word uses at least two colors. Weighted Cauchy-Schwarz gives Σ_αN_α²/binom(n;α)>=(ΣN_α)²/Σbinom(n;α)=q_n²/3^n. Multiply by six.

Cauchy-Schwarz gives |X_π|<=||f||²=q_n. Therefore X_π²<=q_n² times the indicator of X_π≠0. Take expectations and apply the preceding second-moment lower bound. The zero event of X_π is exactly that of A_n.

results.claim: Using the a.a.s. 3-colorability result quoted in the supplied source, Pr[A_n=0]=Pr[N_+=N_->0]+o(1). Thus the unresolved target is precisely anti-concentration of the signed color-orbit imbalance.
results.proof_sketch: The orbit formula says A_n=0 exactly when N_+=N_-. If the graph is not 3-colorable, both are zero; the supplied result makes this event o(1). On a colorable graph equality means a genuine cancellation with both counts positive. Splitting according to colorability proves the statement.
